newsitem.title: UK: Bulgarian Bradies buoyant on IMF funding accord.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian Bradies buoyant on IMF funding accord.

text.p: Brady bond buyers reacted positively to news of an IMF funding accord in Bulgaria on Monday, driving prices higher in an otherwise subdued market, dealers said.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and Bulgaria's interim cabinet announced an accord on financial reform and funding worth more than $650 million to stabilise the shattered economy over the next year.
The Bulgaria FLRB BGFLIRB=RR rose 5/8 to 45-5/8 bid at 1515 GMT.
Russia was also attracting attention after new government appointments in the country, but traders said prices were easing in light trade.
Russian president Boris Yeltsin has announced a government reshuffle, reasserting his power after months of illness.
"These are positives for the Eastern European region," an emerging market analyst said.

He said the market would be watching Yeltsin ahead of this week's summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton in the Finnish capital Helsinki. "People will be watching Yeltsin's state of health and how he comes across."
Dealers said there had only been light trading in Russian brady debt.
Russia dollar Vnesh was marginally off by 1/8 at 81-5/8 bid at 1515 GMT.
"Until all the new (Russian) government appointments are known, it is a little bit early for the market to react in a very strong way," a dealer said.
Other dealers said the U.S. interest rate outlook was still the key concern.
